title: Diwali 2026 Recipes: Nine Traditional Dishes and the Kaju Sweets to Make at Home
excerpt: From chakli and bhakarwadi to rasmalai and kaju katli, NDTV Food's festive lists — plus a full cashew katli recipe — for Diwali on Sunday, November 8.
body:
• Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8, in a five-day festival that begins with Dhanteras on November 6 and ends with Bhai Dooj on November 11.
  • NDTV Food's nine traditional recipes span the full festive table: cashew barfi, chakli, coconut barfi, rasmalai, sandesh, phirni, dahi bhalla, sev-chivda and bhakarwadi.
  • Cashew sweets lead the mithai box again this year, and kaju katli — the most gifted Diwali sweet — can be made at home from six ingredients; the full recipe is in the card below.
  • Plan by shelf life: dry faral snacks such as chakli, sev-chivda and bhakarwadi keep one to two weeks in airtight jars, so make them before Dhanteras and leave milk sweets like rasmalai and phirni for the final two days.

Diwali cooking has a fixed calendar this year. The festival of lights falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, with the five-day celebration running from Dhanteras on November 6 to Bhai Dooj on November 11, according to festival guides tracking the 2026 dates. For home cooks, that leaves a clear runway — and NDTV Food's list of nine traditional Diwali recipes covers the dishes that anchor the festive table, from Maharashtrian faral to Bengali mithai.

The Nine Traditional Recipes

The list opens with cashew barfi, the diamond-shaped cashew-and-milk sweet that, in NDTV Food's words, takes mithai shops by storm during Diwali — and can be prepared at home in less than an hour. Chakli follows: a crispy rice-flour snack, deep-fried and known as murukku in South India, made in large numbers in Maharashtra for Diwali and Narak Chaturdashi. Coconut barfi, made with fresh coconut flakes, khoya, ghee and sugar, is the third sweet on the list.

The milk-based classics come next. Rasmalai — chenna discs in cardamom-flavoured milk — is described as an all-time favourite that works as a festive dessert year-round. Sandesh brings Bengal to the table, made from sweetened cottage cheese flavoured with cardamom and kesar. Phirni, the ground-rice and milk pudding served chilled, carries pistachios and elaichi. The savoury side closes the nine: dahi bhalla, fluffy lentil dumplings under sweetened curd, chutneys and chaat masala; sev-chivda, the cereal, sev, dried fig and wafer mix that is an essential part of the Maharashtrian Diwali faral; and bhakarwadi, gram-flour spirals stuffed with coconut, sesame and poppy seeds that are indispensable to Gujarati Diwali celebrations.

"Chakli follows: a crispy rice-flour snack, deep-fried and known as murukku in South India, made in large numbers in Maharashtra for Diwali and Narak Chaturdashi."

Why Kaju Sweets Lead the Mithai Box

NDTV Food's companion festive list is devoted entirely to kaju — cashew — sweets, and the centrepiece is kaju katli. Festival recipe collections call it the most gifted sweet of Diwali: smooth, diamond-shaped and made from premium cashews. The family extends beyond katli to rolls and pedas built on the same cashew base, but katli remains the benchmark against which mithai boxes are judged, and the one sweet diaspora families most often try to reproduce when a good halwai is not nearby.

Make It at Home: Kaju Katli

The full kaju katli method in the recipe card below turns on three details. Grind the cashews to a fine powder but do not over-grind, or the fat releases and the mixture turns oily. Cook the sugar syrup to a one-string consistency before the cashew powder goes in on very low heat. And roll the dough thin — 3 to 4 millimetres — before applying silver vark and cutting the diamonds. The batch yields about 25 pieces and keeps in an airtight box.

For Diaspora Kitchens

The practical order of work matters more than the menu. Dry snacks — chakli, sev-chivda, bhakarwadi — hold for one to two weeks in airtight containers at room temperature, so they can be finished before Dhanteras on November 6. Ghee sweets such as barfi keep three to seven days, while milk sweets and puddings, including rasmalai and phirni, should be refrigerated and made within a day or two of serving. Cooked in that order, a nine-dish Diwali table is achievable in a US or UK kitchen without a single all-day session — and the mithai box for neighbours can be packed from the same batches.

author: Diaspora Desk

steps: Grind cashews in a dry blender to a fine powder. Sieve to remove any coarse pieces. Do not over-grind or the fat will release and make it oily.
In a heavy pan, combine sugar and water. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Cook to a one-string consistency.
Reduce heat to very low. Add cashew powder, stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook for 6-8 minutes until the mixture comes together as a soft dough and leaves the sides of the pan.
Add cardamom powder. Turn off heat.
Transfer to a greased surface. Cool until warm enough to handle. Knead gently for 1-2 minutes.
Roll out to 3-4mm thickness using a rolling pin. Apply silver vark if desired.
Cut into diamond shapes using a sharp knife. Cool completely before removing. Store in an airtight box.
